sources.title: DAVE THE DIVER DLC ‘Subnautica 2 Content Pack’ announced
sources.text: MINTROCKET has announced DAVE THE DIVER ‘s final downloadable content pack—a Subnautica 2 -themed expansion in partnership with Unknown Worlds Entertainment . It will launch free of charge in early 2027. “For our final [downloadable content] expansion, we wanted to create something that felt especially meaningful, and a Subnautica collaboration is what players have been asking us about for a long time,” said MINTROCKET studio director Jaeho Hwang in a press release. “Both games are set underwater, but Subnautica has such a distinct approach to underwater exploration, so working with the Subnautica 2 team gave us a chance to bring a new wave to DAVE THE DIVER experience. We’re really excited for players to see what we’ve been working on, and we hope this collaboration gives them one more fresh and surprising adventure with Dave and his friends, old and new.” Subnautica 2 creative director Anthony Gallegos added, “We’re so excited to collaborate with the team at MINTROCKET. It’s clear that we both adore one another’s games a lot, and the expansion is a love letter to both DAVE THE DIVER and the Subnautica universe. People are in for a treat.” The free expansion will see players explore the strange new waters of Proteus, filled with unfamiliar creatures and valuable resources waiting to be discovered. The upcoming Subnautica 2 Content Pack creates a confluence of mysterious waters unlike anything before, with Dave and Bancho traveling interdimensionally to make new discoveries, unlock strange and exotic recipes, and lend a hand to new friends in need—all while facing periodic confrontations with the perilous Leviathan. DAVE THE DIVER is available now for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , Switch 2 , PlayStation 4 , Xbox One , Switch , PC via Steam , Epic Games Store , and Microsoft Store , iOS, and Android.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Subnautica 2 fans can finally hunt and kill those pesky Nibbler Mangos—in Dave the Diver's crossover DLC
sources.text: I will kill them. I will cook them. I will serve them. Thanks, Dave. It took a while but there's finally an official way to hunt and kill some of Subnautica 2's most annoying sea creatures. The only catch is, you'll have to do it in Dave the Diver DLC—though as catches go, that's a pretty fun one. The crossover was announced today at the Triple-I Initiative showcase. Coming in early 2027, the Dave the Diver X Subnautica 2 content pack will suck Dave into the alien waters of Unknown Worlds' survival game where he can mine resources, hunt fish, and—one would hope—discover some tasty new sushi recipes for Bancho to cook up. Here's the trailer: What caught my eye even more than the glimpse of a massive and intimidating boss at the end of the trailer were those pesky Nibbler Mangos, which start biting you the second you dive into Subnautica 2 and never really stop. Players having no way to kill large enemies in Subnautica 2 has been a bit of a controversy , with some even resorting to mods so they can fight back. It's nice that players can finally get a bit of revenge against those relentless fish, albeit in another game. "We're thrilled to see Subnautica 2's creatures, including the Nibbler Mango, join Dave's world," Mintrocket told PC Gamer via email. "The team had a lot of fun bringing these creatures into our game, and players can expect the DLC to play just like the Dave the Diver they know and love." As for those saddened to hear this is the final DLC for Dave the Diver, that doesn't necessarily mean it's the definitive end of his adventures. "While this will be the final major DLC for Dave the Diver, there may still be smaller content updates or collaborations based on player feedback and our internal plans," Mintrocket told PC Gamer. "Since we're not moving straight into a sequel, we'll keep thinking about ways to make sure players don't forget Dave and his friends." Bancho the Chef, meanwhile, is getting his own game , a prequel, though a release date has yet to be announced. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Chris started playing PC games in the 1980s, started writing about them in the early 2000s, and (finally) started getting paid to write about them in the late 2000s. Following a few years as a regular freelancer, PC Gamer hired him in 2014, probably so he'd stop emailing them asking for more work. Chris has a love-hate relationship with survival games and an unhealthy fascination with the inner lives of NPCs. He's also a fan of offbeat simulation games, mods, and ignoring storylines in RPGs so he can make up his own. sources.title: Cyberpunk 2077 live-action film in development at Paramount Pictures [Update]
sources.text: Paramount Pictures is developing a live-action film set in CD Projekt RED ‘s Cyberpunk 2077 universe, according to a Deadline report . G.I. Joe and Transformers film series producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura will produce the movie alongside CD Projekt RED. The film will be set in the Cyberpunk 2077 universe, though specific story details have not been announced. Update 4:00 p.m.: In a tweet , CD Projekt RED co-CEO Michal Nowakowski added, “We’re excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise. We look forward to sharing more details at the appropriate time.”

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film reportedly in development, with CD Projekt Red collaborating with Paramount to make it
sources.text: UPDATE 12PM BST: CD Projekt Red seems to have confirmed the partnership and film, with joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski commenting on X that: "We're excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise. We look forward to sharing more details at the appropriate time." ORIGINAL STORY 11:40AM BST: A live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film is reportedly in the works at Paramount Pictures. Producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura - a former Warner Bros. exec influential in signing the The Matrix and Harry Potter films, and known for producing the Transformers films - is said to be attached to the project, with CD Projekt Red collaborating. The report comes from Deadline , though the publication had no further information to share than what's above. CD Projekt Red told us it doens't have anything to share beyond what Nowakowski said on X. Believing that CD Projekt Red would venture into live-action film territory doesn't take a stretch of the imagination. The company's Netflix anime partnership on Cyberpunk Edgerunners has been a success, with a second series due to air this month, on 20th October . The first season, released in 2022, was "fantastic", Wes wrote in his Cyberpunk Edgerunners impressions article , and amassed considerable Netflix viewing figures . Live-action adaptations of video game-based series are also becoming increasingly popular, with The Last of Us and Fallout particularly finding wide success. CD Projekt Red being involved with the Cyberpunk 2077 adaptation would also somewhat heal a wound left by not being involved with The Witcher Netflix adaptation. CD Projekt art director Pawel Mileniczuk called this a "missed opportunity" when I talked to him for a Witcher 3 10-year anniversary article last year. Meanwhile, CD Projekt Red is working on Cyberpunk 2 , a project that's in pre-production, but with an expanding team - close to 200 people as of 31st July 2026 - full production doesn't seem far away. The sequel apparently adds a second city alongside the iconic Night City setting, and it's described as being like "Chicago gone wrong". Should the live-action film prove real, and be made, the questions are what story will it tell - the same as in Cyberpunk 2077? - and which actors will play the game's well-known roles? The most famous of those roles is Keanu Reeves' portrayal of Johnny Silverhand, a character who used Reeves' likeness in the game. Could Reeves star in a film adaptation? Cyberpunk 2077 was released in 2021 , and its rocky launch has since become infamous. But CD Projekt Red did extensive work improving the game after release, focusing its efforts around a kind of 2.0 relaunch alongside the game's "remarkable" Phantom Liberty expansion , in 2023. Paramount, meanwhile, recently acquired Warner Bros., and has since reorganised into mega-company Skydance. Activision's former leader Bobby Kotick has been employed on the board of it .

sources.title: Ghost of Tsushima: Legends anime delayed to 2028
sources.text: The anime series based on the Sucker Punch Productions -developed PlayStation game Ghost of Tsushima: Legends , which was previously planned to debut in 2027, which will now premiere on Crunchyroll in 2028, Aniplex and Crunchyroll announced . Mayumi Saco and Shinya Fukumatsu will join the cast of the show in undisclosed role. Saco previously voiced Tomoe in the original game, while while Fukumatsu is known for portraying Bomb in One-Punch Man . The anime is being directed by Takanobu Mizuno at studio Kamikaze Douga, with Gen Urobuchi writing the story composition and co-writing the script with Renji Oki. New staff members include composer Keiji Inai, sound director Yoshikazu Iwanami, sound editor Yasumasa Koyama, and title calligraphy artist Gyousyou Suzuki. Ghost of Tsushima: Legends is produced by HAYATE in collaboration with Aniplex and PlayStation Productions, with Sony Music serving as music and soundtrack partner.

sources.title: Ghost of Tsushima anime arrives in 2028 as OG game actor joins cast
sources.text: Ghost of Tsushima Legends has been delayed The upcoming Ghost of Tsushima anime has received a disappointing release date update alongside news of new cast and behind-the-scenes arrivals. At New York Comic Con, Crunchyroll revealed that Ghost of Tsushima Legends is now set for 2028, a slight pushback from its original 2027 window. Two actors, Mayumi Skco and Shinya Fukumatsu, were also confirmed to join the cast. If you've played Ghost of Tsushima in Japanese, you may recognize Saco's voice – she portrayed turncoat villain Tomoe in 2020's Ghost of Tsushima game. It is unknown who the pair will be portraying in Legends, however. Ghost of Tsushima is a 2020 open world adventure charting the revenge journey of Jin Sakai on the Japanese island of Tsushima during feudal times. It was followed up in 2024 by Ghost of Yotei, offering players a new quest as the katana-wielding Atsu hunted down the fearsome Yotei Six after the murder of her parents. In truth, we probably should have expected the delay. We've heard precious little about Ghost of Tsushima Legends since its announcement way back in January 2025. "The Ghost of Tsushima anime will offer fans an exciting new way to experience the game in an anime style that will be bold and groundbreaking," Crunchyroll president Rahul Purini, said at the time in a statement. PlayStation Productions head Asad Qizilbash added, "Ghost of Tsushima’s rich, immersive world and its fantastical Legends mode based on Japanese mythology provide the perfect canvas for this project, and Aniplex is the perfect partner to translate Sucker Punch Productions’ hit video game into a stunning new anime series." stories.title: YouTuber's Channel Permanently Banned Over Censored Hellraiser: Revival Gameplay Video
stories.summary: A YouTuber and streamer's channel was permanently banned for a Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival gameplay video.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: YouTuber's Channel Permanently Banned Over Censored Hellraiser: Revival Gameplay Video
sources.text: A YouTuber and streamer's channel was permanently banned for a Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival gameplay video. French content creator J0nathan said that despite covering up the nudity in the game’s opening scenes with black boxes, his channel was removed for violating YouTube’s sex and nudity policy. “Explicit content that’s meant to be sexually gratifying isn’t allowed on YouTube,” the company told the streamer in response to an appeal upholding the ban. Hellraiser: Revival, from Space Marine 2 developer Saber Interactive, opens with a raunchy sex scene featuring a topless woman and some BDSM play. Following that, the male character runs around for a while with their wang in the wind. While the scene is explicit, it’s essential to understanding the story and acts as the catalyst for everything that follows. J0nathan claimed that this is the scene that got his channel banned, despite the fact uncensored gameplay of the same scene remains live on other YouTube channels. While he did add the "Not Made for Kids" label to the video, he did not age gate it, assuming that censoring the explicit scenes would be enough to satisfy YouTube. "Since the rest of the game was just a standard horror title like Resident Evil I figured it didn't really require an age restriction, and that if anything, YouTube would just apply one later on like they always do," he said. J0nathan had 190,000 subscribers on his channel at the time of the ban, which he told IGN was "permanent." "My channel has been completely deleted, wiping out 10 years of hard work and destroying my main source of income," he continued. "I've never had any issues with the platform before. No warnings, no strikes, nothing. And yet they just threw me away like I was nothing.” J0nathan said he has made attempts to run through YouTube’s appeal process, but “everything seems to be handled by AI.” His first appeal was rejected within a few minutes, and support accounts on social media responded with a generic message: "We've reviewed your case and are upholding our decision.” “How can they possibly uphold such a decision when other videos showing the exact same scene without any censorship are still available on the platform?” he commented. “It really doesn't feel like any human being is actually reviewing these cases.” J0nathan has a side channel but is afraid of using it because YouTube prohibits banned users from operating other channels. If he attempted it, he would run the risk of losing both channels. “I'm absolutely devastated,” he told IGN. “Beyond losing my income, I'm also losing 10 years of hard work and over 3,000 videos. The emotional impact is huge. Those videos represent a big part of my life, and losing them hurts more than I can describe. “I've tried everything. I've reached out to my contacts, asked fellow content creators for help, but none of them have managed to get in touch with anyone at YouTube who could actually review my case. The same goes for the game developers. I've sent them emails and tagged them on X, hoping they might step in and help. I'm convinced they have contacts at YouTube to help prevent unfair bans related to their game, and yet they've completely ignored me.” Ahead of Hellraiser's release, Saber tweeted to offer guidance to content creators concerned that their videos of the game would be at best demonetized, at worst get their channel deleted. Saber recommended content creators label all streams and videos with "appropriate age restrictions, sexual theme labels, and other necessary platform tools." "You will need to adhere to each platform's community guidelines," Saber continued. There is no 'streamer mode,' Saber also pointed out on social media ahead of launch, "so context and intent behind your content will matter." IGN has asked Saber Interactive for comment. Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Hellraiser: Revival review
sources.text: How do you revive a series like Hellraiser? When your source material spans four decades and multiple mediums, all with wildly differing tones (and fans), what stays, what goes? Where would you even begin? It's a question developer Saber Interactive seems to struggle with throughout Hellraiser: Revival and the result is a messy, uneven, but earnest, and often fascinating sort of tribute that, boldly, goes back to the start. Clive Barker's 1986 novella The Hellbound Heart, the genesis of the Hellraiser series, is a queer horror classic; a story of obsession and addiction, loosely inspired by the gay BDSM scene. Later Hellraiser movies would see the series devolve into silliness, iconic villain Pinhead (played by Doug Bradley, who briefly returns here) becoming a quipping counterpart to the Freddies and Chuckies of the time. But Saber seems to have more literary ambitions, drawing heavily on Barker's original themes for its tale of two lovers and their encounter with the Cenonbites; extradimensional beings from a realm where agony and ecstasy are interwined. It's a story that starts with sweaty softcore sex and soon descends into flesh-ripping violence, setting protagonist Aiden against a quasi-religious, extreme BDSM cult as he desperately attempts to rescue his girlfriend Sunny back from Hell. Unfortunately, their relationship is so immediately toxic, it's hard to get emotionally invested in this critical narrative throughline. Tonally, Hellraiser is a strange game. Instead of artfully orchestrated scares, Revival's horrors rely on a grim procession of fused and rended flesh, as relentless as it is effectively offputting. But the ceaseless bodily destruction sits awkwardly alongside villains so deliriously flamboyant, they'd be twiddling their moustaches if it weren't for their masks. And attempts at eroticism and sensuality quickly short circuit amid the dildo-strewn nightclub neon, where extras spit out porn-calibre line readings of flat innuendo. Narratively, it's also a bit of a mess; too obvious and too incoherent by turns, clumsily walking through a minefield of complex ideas - most obviously, the intersection of sex and violence - with all the subtly and nuance of a double-A FPS with an interactive paddle spanking scene. But to its credit, it just about manages to avoid feeling exploitative, and there is, I think, an earnestness to Revival that carries it through. This is the work of a studio, you sense, with a genuine love of the source material - and a desire to do it justice too. And that manifests in a game willing to take some unexpectedly big swings. They don't always work, but at least it's interesting. Take combat, for instance. Revival is, foundationally at least, a fairly bog standard FPS, and it's not long before an early dalliance with perfunctory stealth makes way for more confrontational action. You start with a pistol and, slowly, your arsenal swells to include a shotgun, a revolver, an SMG, and more; an enigmatic old woman intermittently setting up stall to sell you new toys and upgrades (it's not the only time Revival feels like it's channeling Resident Evil 4 ). Eventually, you're mowing down the Unworthy armed with laser-sight pointers and incendiary shells, which should be the absolute antithesis of horror, but Saber just about makes it work. For starters, Aiden moves with a satisfying sense of physicality. He wobbles when he runs, sidesteps with weighty momentum, and, when the melee weapons come out, he bludgeons and slices with sickeningly tangible abandon. And while Revival is undoubtedly action-heavy, Saber still finds tension in withholding. Weapons break, ammo is short, and even the most basic enemies take a good few hits to bring down. Throw in armoured foes which need to be stripped first - either with a swing of something heavy or a particularly aggressive blast - and every combat encounter feels like it's perpetually teetering on the brink of disaster. But Revival strikes a good balance between stressful and unduly punishing. And while I don't love the modern day proliferation of crafting systems, the focus on furious scavenging here feels additive. It heightens the sense of last-gasp desperation as you pocket anything and everything, in the hope you've got enough to eke out a couple more health packs or bullets when things go wrong. Your limited inventory space, meanwhile, forces some tough choices as you frantically shuffle, stash, or abandon items, optimistically Tetrising together the most effective arsenal from the scraps at your disposal. Later, Hellraiser's iconic puzzle box - here, the Genesis Configuration - essentially becomes a gravity gun, so you can fling sawblades, spikes, even fireballs, shredding through multiple bodies as one. And if you're short on the Suffering needed to power it, near-dead enemies wobble on their last legs so you can gruesomely syphon it out of them. Combat's pilfered parts might feel Resident Evil by way of Half-Life and Doom, but at its best, Hellraiser finds an enjoyably ad hoc rhythm of its own - creating showdowns of pure frantic panic as you scramble to juggle weapons that seem to empty their ammo in seconds, as you furiously scan your surroundings for something pointy to use as a projectile, and delve into your inventory, desperately jettisoning stuff to make space for whatever feels most pressing right now. The trouble is Revival spends a lot of time failing to make the most of its tools. Particularly in the first half of the game, progress feels like a linear sequence of encounters that are over before they've even begun, so quick to wrap up there's no space to settle into anything like a rewarding combat rhythm. (Conversely, bosses tend to drag on a touch too long.) And it tends to make for a lot of uninspiring busywork in a game that's already erratically paced, often adopting the relaxed meandering of a walking sim. sources.title: Hellraiser: Revival Gameplay Gets YouTuber Permanently Banned
sources.text: A YouTuber has had their channel permanently banned from their platform for showcasing Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival gameplay that featured blurred explicit content. The YouTuber in question goes by xj0nathan on X (formerly Twitter) and has informed players about the issue. He has been running his YouTube channel for over 10 years and has built a subscriber base of 190,000 during that time. However, one particular gameplay video from Saber Interactive’s latest title appears to have erased all those years of hard work. Spotted by IGN , On September 23, xj0nathan revealed on X that their YouTube video about Hellraiser: Revival had been removed from the platform due to “nudity.” A few days later, their channel was also deleted. The creator explained that the video contained an hour of content and included a short scene that had been blurred. Despite this, their channel was still taken down, while several other users still had similar content on their channels without any censorship. Just yesterday, the creator posted another update with a screenshot of a response from YouTube. The response stated, “We have reviewed your content and found severe or repeated violations of our sex and nudity policy,” so they removed the channel. The response also stated, “Explicit content that’s meant to be sexually gratifying isn’t allowed on YouTube.” xj0nathan has tried to argue his case multiple times, but to no avail. He has received that this was the first violation he has received, and he also argued that the content they are classifying as sexual gratification was only a short scene out of a 1-hour gameplay video, which was censored too. The latest post on X (formerly Twitter) from the creator calls for YouTube to conduct “one final serious review” of his case. He stated that if this doesn’t happen, he will have to consider pursuing appeals under the DSA framework and may initiate legal proceedings with his lawyer. What are your thoughts on a YouTuber being permanently banned for showcasing Hellraiser: Revival gameplay? sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: After Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Daredevil star Charlie Cox is in a new Sega game
sources.text: After dipping his toes into gaming with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, Daredevil star Charlie Cox says he's working on an upcoming Sega game. After over 20 years of acting, Cox finally made his game debut in 2025's Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 as lead character Gustave. And despite only spending four hours working on the French JRPG (or J'RPG if you will), the game blew up and unexpectedly became one of his most beloved roles in the long acting career. On top of that, the Cox noted that the game "has seemingly opened a new avenue for my professional work" as he confirmed he was working on another game earlier this year. At New York Comic Con 2026, Cox spoke to IGN (below) and revealed a little more about his upcoming game, explaining, "I did another one, it doesn't have a name yet," and revealing that "I did a Sega one." He adds: "It hasn't come out yet but it was fun to do." Cox continues, "It's hard. It's a whole different job," explaining, "I had to do, like, 40 hours," which is obviously a bit more intensive than his four hours on Clair Obscur. With it not even having a name, naturally details are scarce, but Cox shares an amusing anecdote that maybe shines a bit more light on the game. "I showed up for the first day, and I was like, 'Hi guys, nice to meet you! How are you?' And all of them went, '...oh, he's English.'" He adds, "they wanted him to be American, but like, now I've got to do 40 hours of lines I've not prepared in an accent." It being so early that it doesn't have a name yet means it's probably something we don't even know about; which is to say RPG fans hoping for Cox to bless Persona 6 with a performance are probably out of luck. Given how much RGG Studio loves casting celebrity actors, I can imagine the studio casting Cox in an upcoming game. With Cox having an American accent in Daredevil, a TV show where he plays a lawyer, I'd maybe have to speculate that perhaps a return of the Judgment series could be in the cards? A year later, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Daredevil star Charlie Cox has finally played the hit J'RPG: "I'm not very good at it." sources.title: Following Nintendo and Sony's lead, Xbox is setting up a division exclusively dedicated to movies and non-games partnerships
sources.text: Today, Microsoft announced it is setting up a new branch of the Xbox business named XP. In a blog over at the Xbox Wire, Microsoft details what this new area of the business looks like - it consists of four branches: Xbox Places, Xbox Pictures, Xbox Partnerships, Xbox Products. "[XP] brings together capabilities that have existed across various teams at Xbox for years and aligns them behind a shared mission: helping our franchises reach more people, create deeper connections with players and new fans, and unlock new opportunities for these fandoms to grow around the world," says a press release from Matthew Ball, chief strategy officer at Xbox. "Great games remain at the center of these franchises and at the heart of Xbox. XP will partner with the best creative minds across our studios, along with trusted partners, to build on that foundation and create more ways for people to experience the worlds they love." A large focus of Microsoft's newest investment will be in cross-media partnerships, looking particularly at film and TV. It seems lots of publishers are eyeing up the film industry, no doubt buoyed by the massive success of titles like the Super Mario Bros. and Super Mario Galaxy movies ( which have earned $1.36bn and $1bn, respectively ) and Sony's recently released Resident Evil movie (which is tracking at $280m+ at the time of writing). Xbox has had its own notable successes on the big screen, too: last year A Minecraft Movie amassed more than $550m (£415m) in two weeks , immediately setting up a sequel . Xbox has also experimented with TV in the past, too. Fallout is the highlight for the company at the moment, with Fallout Season 2 boasting 83 million viewers tuning in during its first 13 weeks of release . Less successful was Paramount's divisive Halo TV show, which was cancelled after two seasons . A question that springs to my mind when reading this is: where will we go next? There are plenty of Xbox franchises that'd make for good TV; Perfect Dark, Fable, and maybe even a Forza story in the style of Sony's peculiar Gran Turismo show would work. I know the initial run at a Halo TV show was a bit of a flop, but I'd love to see a limited series on the Fall of Reach. It'd make some fine prestige television. We know there's a Gears of War film and a Sea of Thieves film in production, too. Elsewhere, there's Xbox Places. This is the arm of the company that'll oversee the Minecraft theme parks that are opening in the US and UK that so far represent over £85m of investment from Mojang and Xbox. They're expected to open 'between 2026 and 2027'. Will we hear about more real-life locations that'll fall under the 'Places' banner? It remains to be seen. All these initiatives will no doubt require staffing, which is such to be a sore subject for any of the staff that have been impacted by wide-ranging cuts at Microsoft and Xbox over the past few years . Given the contraction of its game studios and software business, is Xbox trying to recoup costs by pursuing other avenues for growth? It certainly seems like it.
